I study how the places we inherit shape the lives we can build. My interests are in urban economics, particularly how spatial and institutional change reshapes people’s opportunities, relationships, and choices.

My developing research agenda, **Urban Memory**, connects these questions to the persistence and transformation of urban life. Current projects examine the Atlanta Streetcar and Oregon’s middle-housing reform.

## Background & interests

I am from Taiyuan, Shanxi, and grew up in Beijing. My background in economics and creative writing informs how I approach both research and teaching. Beyond economics, I enjoy reading history and poetry, writing, and photography. I am drawn to restrained expression, the passage of time, and the details through which ordinary places acquire meaning.
